https://cbn.co.za/industry-news/expos-ev.text: Demand for EVs continues its growth across Europe and South Africa with Chinese brands increasing market share, new OLX data shows Every electric vehicle market tracked by OLX Group ("OLX") is still growing at double- or triple-digit rates, and Chinese automotive brands are capturing a growing share of that demand, according to new data published recently. OLX, a global online classifieds leader with nearly 60 million daily listings across seven markets, has today published The Great Acceleration: East Meets Electric, which examines consumer demand for electric vehicles across five OLX automotive marketplaces: La Centrale (France), Autovit (Romania), Standvirtual (Portugal), Otomoto (Poland), and AutoTrader (South Africa). The data shows EV adoption maturing into a structural trend rather than a short-term reaction: every market measured has now sustained double- or triple-digit year-on-year EV lead growth, even as these growth rates ease from previously seen highs. Chinese automotive brands remain central to that story, with MG and BYD now among the leading Chinese brands in four of the five markets, as manufacturers continue to expand the availability of EVs at accessible price points. Key findings Every tracked market posted double- or triple-digit year-on-year EV lead growth in June 2026: France up +206%, South Africa up +154.6%, Romania up +66.0%, Portugal up +60.0%, and Poland up +34.3%. Portugal remains Europe's most EV-mature market, with EVs accounting for 14.9% of leads, almost double the next closest market. France remains the fastest-growing EV market in the group and the one where EV prices are still climbing (+25% year-on-year). MG and BYD are now the most consistently dominant Chinese brands across the group, appearing among the leading brands in France, Romania, Portugal and Poland. Christian Gisy, CEO of OLX, said: "The story our data tells is straightforward: where EV adoption is accelerating, demand for Chinese automotive brands is accelerating with it. That is no coincidence — Chinese manufacturers are actively expanding the market, bringing electric vehicles to consumers at lower price points than ever before. This means EVs are now more accessible for more people. The transition to electric mobility is happening faster, and more broadly, because Chinese manufacturers are in it." EV demand remains strong Consumer interest in EVs remains high across all five markets, with every market recording double- or triple-digit year-on-year growth in EV leads. France leads at +206%, followed by South Africa at +154.6%, Romania at +66%, Portugal at +60%, and Poland at +34.3%. Portugal remains the most mature EV market, with electric vehicles accounting for close to one in seven leads on the platform (14.9%). The report finds that demand, which surged in the months following the outbreak of the conflict in Iran in February 2026 as fuel costs and energy security became more prominent considerations for consumers, has since settled into a steadier, sustained pattern consistent with structural adoption rather than a short-term reaction. Chinese automotive brands are helping unlock EV growth As EV demand matures, Chinese automotive brands are moving from early experimentation to a phase where a smaller number of manufacturers are converting early interest into durable market share. MG and BYD now feature among the leading Chinese brands in four of the five markets tracked. France recorded the strongest increase in consumer demand for Chinese automotive brands, rising +276% year-on-year — more than double the next-fastest market, Romania (+119%). Portugal (+74%) and Poland (+95%) also recorded strong increases as Chinese manufacturers continued to expand their presence. Chinese manufacturers continue to adapt to local market conditions. In Romania, where EV prices declined nearly 8% year-on-year, the increased availability of Chinese-made vehicles continues to expand access to more affordable electric vehicles. This differs from France, where consumer interest in Chinese automotive brands keeps growing despite a +25% increase in EV prices, reflecting sustained demand in a supply-constrained market. Chinese manufacturers adapt to local market dynamics While EV demand is strong across all five OLX markets, the report shows Chinese manufacturers continuing to adapt their vehicle offering, pricing and market positioning to reflect each market's stage of EV adoption. Portugal, Europe's most mature EV market, continues to show Chinese brands competing on technology and model choice as much as price, with Xpeng now among the leading brands alongside MG and BYD. Poland remains the group's most diversified Chinese brand market by brand count, with MG, BYD and Omoda leading. South Africa represents a different stage of market development. Chinese brands account for the highest share of demand in the group (7.31%), led by Haval, but that demand is concentrated on petrol and hybrid SUVs rather than EVs – just 0.3% of Chinese brand demand there is electric. This reflects the influence of local infrastructure, driving conditions and consumer preferences, with Chinese manufacturers adapting their approach to each market rather than pursuing a single strategy across all five. “The +154.6% increase in EV leads shows that interest in electric mobility is growing rapidly in South Africa, even from a relatively small base,” commented George Mienie, CEO of AutoTrader South Africa. “Chinese manufacturers are helping drive this shift by offering vehicles that respond well to local priorities around affordability, technology, and practicality.” Methodology All figures are drawn from leads-based consumer activity across OLX Group's five automotive marketplace platforms. La Centrale (France), Autovit (Romania), Standvirtual (Portugal), Otomoto (Poland) and AutoTrader (South Africa). "Leads" refers to meaningful user engagement: views, enquiries, and contact events. Data is as at 30 June 2026. Full methodology is available in the report.

https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/body-foun.text: Nadeem Badshah Updated Sat, August 15, 2026 at 5:37 PM UTC 0 His family said Smyth ‘was the best of us and is deeply missed by his younger brothers, family and friends’,Photograph: Family handout via Salvamont Brașov A body has been found in the search for an 18-year-old British man who went missing last year while hiking in Romania, UK police said. George Smyth, a geology student at the University of Bristol, went missing in November. On Saturday, Avon and Somerset police said a body found in the region of the country is believed to be that of Smyth. His family have been informed and are being supported by a family liaison officer, the force added. Smyth’s family said: “We are all devastated by George’s death. “He was the best of us and is deeply missed by his younger brothers, family and friends. “We want to thank Salvamont mountain rescue, who have worked tirelessly since November searching for George, despite very difficult and often dangerous conditions. “They are an amazing team, and have remained in constant communication, helping us greatly throughout this awful time.” Efforts will be made to return Smyth’s body to the UK once formal identification has taken place. The family’s statement added: “We would also like to thank Avon and Somerset police and University of Bristol, who have gone above and beyond to try and find George, and to support us as a family. “Although this latest news is incredibly painful, the torture of waiting is finally over, so we can now focus on bringing George home and saying goodbye. “We would appreciate privacy while we continue to come to terms with this loss.” On Wednesday, mountain rescue teams said they had resumed their search in “previously indicated areas, under rock walls, in grates and in the hard-to-reach sectors” but without success. The student, from Newport in Shropshire, is believed to have left Poiana Brașov heading to Bran. He reached Țigănești, where he made an emergency call for help. At the time, rescuers said he was in a “very isolated and hard to access mountain area” and the weather conditions were extremely severe with strong winds, heavy snowfall and dense fog. The search and rescue operation also involved a canine unit, drones and helicopters being deployed. Sebastian Marinescu, from the area’s mountain rescue service, previously told the BBC the 18-year-old “was disoriented, physically exhausted, and already showing signs of hypothermia” when they received the emergency call. Photograph: Roberto Monaldo/LaPresse/Shutterstock Opinion The far right Radical-right youth groups are at the root of Europe’s populist surge Cas Mudde and Duncan McDonnell From France’s Jordan Bardella to Italy’s Giorgia Meloni, organised youth politics has produced many rightwing leaders. Democrats must catch up Mon 2 Nov 2026 00.00 EST Last modified on Mon 2 Nov 2026 05.16 EST Share T he leaders of the most successful populist radical right parties in western Europe have one thing in common that is often overlooked. Italy’s Matteo Salvini , Jordan Bardella from France, Jimmie Åkesson from the Sweden Democrats, and Tom Van Grieken from Belgium’s Vlaams Belang all led the youth wing of the parties they now run. These movements shaped the politicians they are today, and they are now shaping Europe’s political future. As Italy’s prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, another former radical right youth-wing leader, put it : “Even more than my growth as a politician, I owe my growth as a person and as an Italian to my youth-wing activism. There is no more formative training ground than this.” And yet, until recently, we knew little about these incubation chambers of populist radical right parties. ‘A direct cultural threat’: your questions on the rise of the right across Europe answered Read more In researching our new book, Youth Wings of the Populist Radical Right , we looked at 10 such organisations from across Europe. From the youth wing of Austria’s Freedom party to that of France’s National Rally, we found they help to recruit, train and promote the radical right’s grassroots members, their representatives and leaders of the future. They also perform important functions for their parties in the present, encouraging young people to vote for them, providing a key source of labour during election campaigns, running party branches and influencing policy. In particular, we found that youth-wing leaders and their rank and file members are helping to achieve three key goals for the radical right as their parties expand in the 2020s: internationalisation, professionalisation and normalisation. First, these youth wings go even further than their older equivalent organisations in building new transnational alliances. Away from the spotlight, there has been a proliferation of international far-right workshops and conferences, such as the Transatlantic Patriot Summit , held each year in Budapest since 2022. These and similar events have brought together youth leaders from Europe, India, Israel, Latin America and the US, to talk about common aims and establish ties that will last through their careers. Many of the youth leaders we spoke to talked openly about how these international ties will benefit them “when we are the ones in government”. View image in fullscreen The National Rally’s Jordan Bardella poses for a selfie with supporters. Photograph: Patrick Hertzog/AFP/Getty Images Second, they are heavily involved in political training at international, national and local levels. Once derided as a bunch of amateurs (and with good reason, in some cases), the populist radical right now invests considerably in professionalisation. The young people who join are taught not only about policies and history, but also rhetoric and media communications. They are being trained as future politicians, and the likes of Åkesson, Bardella, Meloni and Salvini are proof of concept. Third, the recruitment of university-educated young people – who look and sound very different from the stereotypical media image of the angry far-right youth – feeds into the growing normalisation of the populist radical right. Producing more articulate, professional and presentable leaders can help their parties be seen by voters as legitimate political actors. And the more distance they can put between themselves and previous generations of uncouth leaders, such as Jean-Marie Le Pen in France or Umberto Bossi in Italy, the more they can attract young people like themselves. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to This is Europe The most pressing stories and debates for Europeans – from identity to economics to the environment after newsletter promotion View image in fullscreen Stickers offered at the refounding of the AfD youth organisation in Giessen, Germany, 29 November 2025. Photograph: Martin Meissner/AP But this smartening up of the radical right’s public image does not reflect a softening of the message. The young leaders we spoke to will not lead their parties down a path to moderation. They may have found ways to smooth down their movements’ rough edges, but the ideology is still an exclusionary, nationalist one. In other words, the regeneration of the radical right through its youth wings makes it an even more significant challenge to liberal democracy. How can mainstream parties respond to this challenge? One way would be to stop focusing on the radical right as the root of their problems, and to look at themselves and their own youth wings. Recent research into youth-wing membership has found that centre-left and centre-right youth groups are dominated by men, people from political families and careerists. If mainstream parties are to regain ground with young people, this needs to change. Governing parties could also do far more to address the problems that young people are facing in the 21st century. For most of the postwar period, younger generations in western Europe grew up with the implicit promise that they would have better life prospects than their parents. That promise has been broken. In fact, with the rise of insecure employment, compounded by the housing crisis, a significant minority of young Europeans are still living with their parents into their late 20s and early 30s. It is no surprise that many have little faith in the capacity of mainstream parties to change their lives. By contrast, the young populist radical-right activists we interviewed talked about how their parties spoke to them in clear terms about the issues that concerned them, and offered them solutions. Mainstream parties should be doing the same. Cas Mudde is the Stanley Wade Shelton UGAF professor of international affairs at the University of Georgia, and author of The Far Right Today ; Duncan McDonnell is professor of politics at the Jeff Bleich Centre in Flinders University in Adelaide, Australia. https://www.portfolio.hu/unios-forrasok/.text: Az új javaslat 204 milliárd euróval csökkentené a kiadásokat az Európai Bizottság által eredetileg felvázolt, 2000 milliárd eurós főösszegű költségvetési tervhez képest. Ez a lépés a takarékos hatok – Németország, Ausztria, Svédország, Finnország, Hollandia és Dánia – követeléseinek próbál eleget tenni, amelyek határozottan szorgalmazták a büdzsé karcsúsítását. Az eredeti tervezet a hagyományos agrártámogatások és kohéziós források mellett eurómilliárdokat különített volna el a védelemre és a versenyképesség javítására. A két legnagyobb uniós tagállam fenntartásokkal fogadta a módosítást. Friedrich Merz német kancellár óvatosan üdvözölte a tervezetet, és jó első lépésnek nevezte, ugyanakkor hangsúlyozta, hogy a kiadások összességében még mindig túl magasak. Véleménye szerint az igazságos tehermegosztáshoz a bevételi oldalon is korrekciókra van szükség. Franciaország ezzel szemben amiatt bírálta a javaslatot, hogy az nem garantálja megfelelően a gazdálkodók jövedelemtámogatását. Emmanuel Macron elnök hivatalának egyik tisztviselője szerint a jelenlegi tervezet nem képezheti megállapodás alapját. A bevételi oldalon is érdemi változás történt, mivel a terv háromszázalékos adót vetne ki a digitális szolgáltatásokat nyújtó nagyvállalatokra. Ez váltaná fel a Bizottság korábbi, a tagállamok többsége által elutasított ötletét, amely egy éves, átalányjellegű társasági adót irányzott elő, a dohánytermékekből származó bevételek megcsapolása és az elektronikai hulladékok utáni illeték mellett. A lépéshez a tagállamoknak egy 2018 óta húzódó digitális adójavaslatot kellene véglegesíteniük, amely eddig az Egyesült Államok nyomása, valamint a technológiai óriásoknak otthont adó országok – például a soros elnökséget jelenleg betöltő Írország – ellenállása miatt akadt el. A 2028 és 2034 közötti időszakra szóló többéves pénzügyi keretet (MFF) hivatalosan csak 2027 végéig kellene elfogadni. António Costa, az Európai Tanács elnöke azonban már az idei év végéig tető alá akarja hozni az alkut, még mielőtt a jövő évi sorsdöntő – többek között franciaországi és lengyelországi – választások befolyásolnák a tárgyalásokat. Costa szerint a mostani javaslat összhangban van az uniós ambíciókkal, és alkalmas a társadalmi kihívások kezelésére. A költségvetés mérete mellett a prioritások is komoly vitákat váltanak ki. Míg a keleti tagállamok a védelmi kiadások növelését sürgetik, mások a hagyományos támogatási területek megtartása mellett érvelnek. A legnagyobb nettó befizetőnek számító Németország részéről Merz kancellár a közelmúltban a kohéziós források kifizetését is az Ukrajnának nyújtott támogatáshoz kötötte. Az uniós állam- és kormányfők a csütörtökön kezdődő kétnapos brüsszeli EU-csúcson vitatják meg az új költségvetési javaslatot. Ennek a cikknek az előkészítésében AI-asszisztens működött közre, a végleges tartalmat újságírónk szerkesztette és ellenőrizte. Mutatjuk, hol vannak a jó beszállók szerinte. Ursula von der Leyen is megszólalt az ügyben. A lépés több milliárdos vagyonra terjed ki. Ma sokan úgy élik meg, hogy az iskolának mindenekelőtt gyermekmegőrző funkciója van. A tárcavezető a legfontosabb prioritásokat és támogatási elveket is felvillantotta. Az USA egyelőre nem reagált az iráni javaslatokra. A vállalkozók saját helyzetük javulását várják, miközben nem számítanak a gazdasági környezet javulására. Akkor mire épül ez a derűlátás? A gazdasági környezet természetes állapota Hagyományos, eredeti értelmében így működött a tőzsdei részvénykibocsátás. Van egy remek ötletem, mondjuk drága keleti fűszereket hajóznék be Európába, ismerek egy jó forrást, olcsón Nem a zsemle kicsi.
